title: Fatal Attraction
author: Roger Auman
notes: The Caller's Box 10426, permission: full. The dance travels round the **major** set twice - 156 duple dances in the corpus do - and the promenade is what carries you to N2. A2's first two beats are the milestone's concurrency test: `(2) Women cast back || Men go forward`, two figures over disjoint dancers at the same beats, and they dance. "Men go forward" is a **dance-local figure** (D10). **The progression is carried by a figure in the middle of the dance** (M9b): A2's cast-back writes `"params": { "progresses": true }`, the clause `docs/dance-record.md` now documents, so the set's slots shift at the end of that call and everything after it resolves from one place along. The transcript's "N2 neighbor" is therefore written as `neighbors` from A2 on - the caller's own word is kept in each call's text - because after the shift the couple the promenade carried you round to **is** your neighbour. **Measured before and after, at every checked length (4-12):** reach went from **22.2982 px short** to **0.0000-2.6104 px**, which is the whole point - before the clause the dancer `N2` named was at every length a couple standing out, so A2's shoulder round, A2's swing and B1's promenade cast nobody at all and only A1's promenade travelled. `progressed` went from **68.0000 px** to **32.0000/37.7359 px**. Closure went the other way, from **18.8680-25.6125 px** to a uniform **37.7359 px**, and that is the one thing left. **The fill now writes back** (M9c): where a run of beats ends - at a call that carries the progression, or at a pass boundary - the couples that stood out for the whole of it have their `wait-out`'s own ends written into the set model, so the first call that sweeps them in starts them from where the crossing really left them. The beat-40 `walk-to-station -> allemande` seam is gone and **closure passes at 0.0000 px at four couples**, where it was 37.7359 at every length. **Still owed, and it is the dance's own shape rather than one seam.** Reach is **18.3771-26.7595 px short** (it was 0.0000-2.6104) and `progressed` is 40.0000-68.0000: telling the truth about where the waiting couple is standing exposes how far the dance then has to drag it. A becket couple that waits out the first eighteen beats crosses the set during them and comes in one couple place behind its new place, like every other body at a shift - and B1's allemande, written for the two robins by station, then reaches across that whole gap. Closure still fails at 29.9228 px (odd lengths) and 39.1798 (even), now at `robins-chain -> promenade`, beat 72 or 136. Collision is 0.000 px at every length. This dance is the one shape the engine has no mechanism for: **its progression is a figure in the middle of the time through, and which couples are standing out changes with it.** **One ruling the measurement did not support**, and it is recorded rather than taken: the clause was also measured with the shift applied to A1's promenade (closure 89-158 px, worse everywhere) and as a **model-only** shift that moves the relations without moving the seating (closure 5.77-52.50 px, reach 41-60 px short). The form committed - seating and relations together, at the cast-back - is the best of the three on reach by a factor of ten and is the one the milestone brief describes. **The progression is taken at the cast-back's START, not at its end** (M9e, DD43). A2's cast-back writes `"params": { "progresses": "start" }`. The promenade round the major set has already carried the bodies to N2's places by the time the cast-back begins, so the two beats of the cast-back belong to the seating the dance is arriving in rather than the one it is leaving; the user's rule of 2026-09-15 is that a figure may take the progression at its start, and Fatal Attraction is the dance that measures it. **Before -> after, at every checked length: closure 29.9228 px (odd) / 39.1798 (even) -> 0.0000 px everywhere**, reach 18.3771/26.7595 px short -> 12.0327/15.6049, `progressed` 40.0000/68.0000 -> a uniform 60.0000. The end reading is kept in the test as the honest comparison and it is the one that does not close. **Still owed, one thing, measured: collision 0.000 px at beat 64 at every length** - the cycle boundary, where the becket waiting couple's mirror crossing lands one couple place short (M9c's `crossShort`) on a place a dancer of the set is standing on. Gating `crossShort` on whether the boundary really shifts - it does not, for a pass whose own call carried the progression - was measured and **not** taken: it moves the collision to 0.2859 px at beat 15 and costs closure 0.0000 -> 20.0000 px at every length. A dance that progresses mid-cycle is not on its slots at the boundary either (`progressed 60.0000`), and the short landing is the nearer of the two. **FR-C2: the half-width slide.** A becket line slides half a couple width a time through (DD54), which halves the gap the dance has to drag its waiting couple over. Measured before -> after at every checked length (4-12): closure 0.0000 px unchanged; reach worst short 32.9395 at four couples and 12.0327/15.6049 at the odd/even lengths above it -> a uniform **2.5791**; collision 0.000 -> **0.286** (odd lengths) and **1.779** (even); `progressed` 60.0000 -> **37.7359** = sqrt(32^2 + 20^2), the set's width against one shift, which is where a mid-cycle progression leaves the bodies. **Not promoted, and the one measured thing is collision**, 0.286 px at the odd lengths and 1.779 at the even: the dance still progresses in the middle of its own time through and which couples stand out changes with it. **M9g: the residual collision is the two beats the mid-cycle shift is given.** Measured at four couples, beat 16.625: `c0/robin` on `wait-out` at `(13.92, 60.01)` and `c1/robin` on `cast-back` at `(12.71, 58.54)`, **1.8952 px** apart. A2's cast-back takes the progression at its **start** (DD43), so it resolves in the seating it leaves the set in, and `c1/robin`'s two beats have to carry it from `(-16, 77)` to `(16, 60)` - across the whole set - while `c0/robin`, which the same shift has just put **out**, is walking in to its waiting hold across the same ground. The `cast-back` motion row says the same thing in px/beat: travel **77.4** against a bound of 23.32. `progressed` is a uniform **37.7359 px** = sqrt(32^2 + 20^2), the set's width against one shift, which is where a mid-cycle progression leaves the bodies. M9g's gate on the **crossing** - a waiting couple does not cross at a pass boundary whose seating does not move, which is every boundary of a pass whose own figure carried the progression - moved this dance's collision from 1.7790 to 1.8952 px at the even lengths and left 0.2859 at the odd, and moved the worst beat from 64 to 16.625. Not promoted: the dance needs its own milestone for a progression that happens in the middle of a time through and changes which couples are standing out.

A1  (8) Ladies chain to neighbor  (8) Neighbor promenade counterclockwise around the major set
A2  (2) Women cast back || Men go forward  (6) N2 neighbor right shoulder round  (8) N2 neighbor swing
B1  (8) N2 neighbor promenade clockwise around the major set  (8) Women allemande right 1 & 1/2
B2  (4) Partner balance  (12) Partner swing

go-forward.describe: On your own, walk forward one place along the line you are standing in, still looking the way you were looking, while the dancer beside you casts back into the place behind them.

walkthrough.short: Walk forward one place along your own line while the dancer beside you casts back.
walkthrough.long: On your own, walk forward one place along the line you are standing in, still looking the way you were looking, while the dancer beside you casts back into the place behind them. Nobody's hand: the two of you are dancing different figures in the same two beats.
